name: Eta Draconis
description: A giant of type G8 III 28.2 parsecs away, 10.5 times the Sun's width: its disc was measured with the Navy Precision Optical Interferometer.

radius.source: Baines et al. (2018), AJ 155, 30, HD 148387: radius 10.53 +/- 0.04 solar radii (Table 5), from the limb-darkened angular diameter 3.47 +/- 0.01 mas (NPOI, Table 4) and the Hipparcos (van Leeuwen 2007) parallax

mass.source: Baines et al. (2018), AJ 155, 30, HD 148387: mass 2.45 +/- 0.1 solar masses (Table 6), from the PARAM Bayesian fit to PARSEC isochrones at the measured temperature; the paper calls its masses estimates only

temperature.source: Baines et al. (2018), AJ 155, 30, HD 148387: effective temperature 5060 +/- 64 K (Table 5), from the angular diameter and the bolometric flux of the SED fit

distance.source: Baines et al. (2018), AJ 155, 30, HD 148387: the Hipparcos (van Leeuwen 2007) parallax the radius was computed with (Table 1), 35.42 +/- 0.09 mas, inverted

text.card: A giant of type G8 III, 28 parsecs away: 10.5 times the Sun's width and 66 times its light.
text.introduction: Its disc spans 3.47 milliarcseconds, which gives 10.53 solar radii and 5,060 K at its surface.
text.locator: Tables 1, 4 and 5, HD 148387: parallax, limb-darkened diameter, radius, Teff

radialVelocity.source: SIMBAD's radial velocity for Gaia DR3 1625209684868707328 (quality A), from 2018A&A...616A...7S; Gaia DR3 measures none
